description:
FOUND s509 (Fable, 2026-10-06) by the review probes for s507c PART TWO; PRE-EXISTING on main fee16466, unchanged by that batch.

REPRODUCER (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/misc/sl.pl; perl 5.40.3 vs main):
  sub g  { (@_)[0, 1] }         my $s7 = g(7, 8, 9);      perl: 8    PCL: 2
  sub h2 { return (@_)[1, 2] }  my $s8 = h2(7, 8, 9);     perl: 9    PCL: 2
RIGHT TODAY (same file): a list slice assigned to a scalar directly -- `my $s = (7, 8, 9)[0, 1]`, `(@a)[0, 1]`, `@a[0, 1]`,
`(sort @a)[-1, 0]`, `(f())[1, 2]`, `(split /,/, "a,b,c")[0, 2]` -- and an ARRAY slice as the last statement
(`sub k { my @x = @_; @x[0, 1] }` gives 8).  So the slice's own scalar rule (its last element) is implemented; what is
missing is the route by which a sub's RETURN VALUE takes its context from the caller for a parenthesised LIST slice: the
slice is built as a list and the caller's scalar context then counts it, as it would an array.

RELATED: #2004 (completed) fixed the scalar context LEAKING INTO `return (LIST)[i]`; this is the opposite direction for a
multi-index slice -- the caller's scalar context must REACH it.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): `./pl2cl` on the two-line reproducer and on `sub k` -- compare what wraps
the slice in the return position (the array-slice spelling is the working sibling: rule 11, route the list slice through
the same context-aware return form).

PRIORITY: low-medium (silent wrong; `return (stat $f)[7, 9]` / `(localtime)[5, 4]` returned from a helper and used in
scalar context is the realistic spelling).

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 64353611) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- as filed and the realistic spelling (silent): `sub g { (@_)[0, 1] } my $s = g(7,8,9)` perl 8 PCL 2 ;
  `return (@_)[1, 2]` perl 9 PCL 2 ; `sub st { return (localtime(0))[5, 4] } my $y = st()` perl 0 (the month) PCL 2.  Right: the array
  slice tail `@x[0, 1]` -> 8, `my $s = (7, 8, 9)[0, 1]` -> 8.
LABEL: silent (already in the subject).

=== DONE (s543e, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21; ONE change with #3100) ===
MEASURED (the task's cheap measurement, taken): `./pl2cl` of `sub g { (@_)[0, 1] }` emits the bare `(p-aref-deref @_ (vector 0 1))` and `return (@_)[1, 2]` `(p-tail-value (p-aref-deref ...))`, while the array-slice sibling `@x[0, 1]` emits `(p-caller-ctx (p-slice-result (p-aslice ...)))`: gen_array_ref_access_form asked only "is my context SCALAR" (p-list-scalar) and never the INHERITED context every other slice asks (_slice_in_context_form's p-slice-result), so the tail handed its VECTOR to the caller's scalar context, which counted it.
FIX: Pl/ExprToCL.pm `_list_slice_in_context_form` -- the list slice takes the slice context rule: SCALAR (p-list-scalar F), INHERIT (p-slice-result F), LIST bare; with #3100's one-index form in list / inherited context.
PROBES: scratch/s543e/p4/tail.pl (~25 shapes: the task's two, `(localtime(0))[5, 4]` both contexts, `return (@_)[0]`, `return @x[0,1]` (control), `return @h{qw(a b)}`, `return (f())[1,0]`, a do block, an if arm, a ternary arm, a multi-statement body, `my ($a, $b) = g()`, `scalar(g())`, `print g()`, `g() + 0`, `if (g())`, an empty `@_`, an index past the end, wantarray inside the list): perl = tree; base wrong on 3 lines.
GUARD: Pl/t/transpile-test-11.t row 11 (lines 4-5), inverse FAILS on the base.  ir-spec §3.2e2, DECIDED ## s543e.


=== CLOSED at MAIN-READY-104 `8959afae` (the reviewing session, 2026-11-21; s543e): with #3100: a list slice in a sub`s tail / `return` follows the caller`s context (its last element in scalar context).  Review probe line l4 / l5: tree = perl.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a LIST SLICE that is a sub's return value gives its element COUNT when the sub is called in scalar context -- `sub g { (@_)[0, 1] } my $s = g(7, 8, 9)` is 2 in PCL, 8 in perl (the slice's last element); the same for `return (@_)[1, 2]`
triage_reason: a list slice as a sub's return value in scalar context
